title: Samuel Little
wiki_lead: Samuel Little (né McDowell; June 7, 1940 – December 30, 2020) was an American serial killer who was convicted of 8 murders and confessed to committing 93 murders, across 19 states, between 1970 and 2005. The FBI's Violent Criminal Apprehension Program has confirmed his involvement in at least 60 murders, the largest number of confirmed victims for any serial killer in American history. Little provided sketches for 26 of his victims, although not all have been linked to known murders. His crime spree stretched across the country, with a concentration of murders in Miami and Los Angeles.
wiki_excerpt:
Samuel Little (né McDowell; June 7, 1940 – December 30, 2020) was an American serial killer who was convicted of 8 murders and confessed to committing 93 murders, across 19 states, between 1970 and 2005. The FBI's Violent Criminal Apprehension Program has confirmed his involvement in at least 60 murders, the largest number of confirmed victims for any serial killer in American history. Little provided sketches for 26 of his victims, although not all have been linked to known murders. His crime spree stretched across the country, with a concentration of murders in Miami and Los Angeles.


Early life
Little was born Samuel McDowell on June 7, 1940, in Reynolds, Georgia. The census from the year Little was born said his mother, Bessie Mae, worked as a maid and that his father was 19-year-old Paul McDowell. Little said that his teenaged mother was a "lady of the night", and that she abandoned him as an infant. Soon after his birth, Little's family moved to Lorain, Ohio, where he was brought up mainly by his grandmother. He attended Hawthorne Junior High School. By his own account, he began having sexual fantasies about strangling women as a child, starting when he saw his kindergarten teacher touch her neck; as a teenager, he collected true crime magazines depicting the strangulation of women.
In 1956, after being convicted of breaking and entering into property in Omaha, Nebraska, Little was held in an institution for juvenile offenders. His mother was listed on the booking card as "whereabouts unknown." Little moved to Florida to live with his mother in the late 1960s. By his own account, he was working at various times as a cemetery worker and an ambulance attendant. He said he then "began traveling more widely and had more run-ins with the law," being arrested in eight states for crimes that included driving under the influence, fraud, shoplifting, solicitation, armed robbery, aggravated assault, and rape. Little took up boxing during his time in prison, referring to himself as a former prizefighter.


Crimes

In 1961, Little was sentenced to three years in prison for breaking into a furniture store in Lorain; he was released in 1964. By 1975, he had been arrested 26 times in eleven states for crimes including theft, assault, attempted rape, fraud, and attacks on government officials. 
In 1982, Little was arrested in Pascagoula, Mississippi, and he faced charges for the murder of 22-year-old Melinda Rose LaPree, who had gone missing in September of that year. A grand jury declined to indict him for her murder. However, while under investigation, Little was extradited to Florida and tried for the murder of 26-year-old Patricia Ann Mount, whose body had been found in September 1982. Prosecution witnesses identified Little in court as a person who had spent time with Mount on the night before her disappearance. Out of mistrust of witness testimonies, Little was acquitted in January 1984.

grok_lead: Samuel Little (June 7, 1940 â December 30, 2020) was an American serial killer recognized by the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) as the most prolific in U.S. history, having confessed to murdering 93 people, predominantly women, between 1970 and 2005 across 19 states. Born Samuel McDowell in Reynolds, Georgia, Little was abandoned as an infant by his teenage mother and raised primarily by his grandmother in Lorain, Ohio, where he exhibited early violent tendencies, including choking urges by age seven or eight. His criminal record began in the 1950s with juvenile offenses like theft and burglary, leading to multiple arrests for assault, rape, and fraud across the country by the 1970s, though he evaded murder convictions until later in life. Little targeted vulnerable women, often sex workers or those struggling with substance abuse, whom he met in bars or on the streets; he would typically render them unconscious with punches before strangling them, disposing of bodies in ways that led many deaths to be misclassified as overdoses or accidents. His first confirmed murder was that of Mary Brosley on January 1, 1971, near Miami, Florida, and his killings continued sporadically for over three decades, fueled by transient lifestyles involving boxing, pool hustling, and odd jobs. By 2012, arrested on a narcotics charge in Kentucky, DNA evidence linked him to three unsolved 1980s homicides in Los Angeles, resulting in his 2014 conviction on three counts of first-degree murder and three consecutive life sentences without parole in California. In 2018, while imprisoned, Little began confessing to additional murders to a Texas Ranger, providing detailed accounts, sketches of victims, and crime scene locations that the FBI's Violent Criminal Apprehension Program (ViCAP) verified in at least 50 cases, with over 60 matches by 2021; the remaining confessions are considered credible but ongoing investigations continue to identify victims and provide closure to families. Little died on December 30, 2020, at age 80 in a Los Angeles-area hospital while in custody, with the cause of death later determined to be heart disease and diabetes, marking the end of one of the longest undetected serial killing sprees in American criminal history.
